per_shot.note: Warm glow lands on the shaft walls, but the serpent is a blown-out tangle of shards; head, body and tail do not separate at play size.
Bloom swallows the head; it reads as a burning crystal cluster with a short tail, not a burrowing serpent with a dangerous end.
Violet crystal crab is a good accent against VEIL amber and the cold spill lands on the rock, but it is small and the jaws barely read.
Faceted body, legs and white teeth read; the jaw is narrow, so the bite is under-sold.
Two white-hot figures are the brightest thing in the chamber and pool light on the floor; clearly made of light.
Strong glow that lands and nice ember sparks, but the upright mannequin pose reads as a benign ghost, not a pursuer.
Ice-cyan flock sits in the CRYOS palette and reads as small winged things, but its own light is lost inside the headlamp beam.
Clean faceted bird silhouettes with glowing cores; spill on the surroundings is indistinguishable from the beam.

top_issues.issue: Long One silhouette collapses into a blown-out clump
top_issues.why: Readable at play size is the first test for a threat; the head is overexposed and the body coils into itself, so it does not read as a serpent.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Lay the body out as a long, spaced chain of segments with the head as a distinct wedge; cap head bloom so the jaw and fangs keep their shape.

top_issues.issue: Kindled pose reads as friendly, not hunting
top_issues.why: A pursuer must read as a threat; standing straight with arms down, they look like idle statues of light.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the white-hot body and floor pooling, but lean the figures forward into a stalking, reaching stance.

top_issues.issue: Mimic is small and its bite is understated
top_issues.why: In the play frame it is a little violet blob; the dangerous end, its jaws, does not register.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Widen the jaw gape and push the tooth highlights so the mouth reads first at play scale.

top_issues.issue: Rimewing light does not visibly land
top_issues.why: The flock is only seen inside the headlamp cone, so its own glow on the ice is indistinguishable from the beam.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each wing a small cyan point light that tints nearby ice, visible when the flock is outside the beam.

protect: Kindled as pure white-hot light pooling on the chamber floor
Mimic violet as a deliberate accent against VEIL amber
Rimewings' ice-cyan faceted look inside the CRYOS palette
Long One's warm glow washing the surrounding rock

per_shot.note: Clear segmented serpent with a pointed, fanged head spanning the gap; the orange glow lands on the rock behind it and it reads at play size.
Chunky faceted segments, a glowing seam per plate and a bright fanged head: low-poly, threatening, very VEIL.
Same violet crab but larger, with open spiked jaws that read in the play frame; cold spill pools on the rock.
Wider gaping jaw with white teeth and a crest spike; a clear biter, though its glow is cold white rather than violet.
Hunched stalkers read as hunters, but their rust-coloured bodies blend into the amber chamber and a dark smudge sits behind them.
Predatory forward lean, crystal hearts and spark trails; the body is matte, not light, so 'made of light' and floor pooling weaken.
Essentially the same as A; the shard-star wings are a touch spikier and the flock's own light is still lost in the beam.
Spiky crystalline wings read as icy and faintly hostile; spill on the ice still comes only from the beam.

top_issues.issue: Kindled are no longer made of light
top_issues.why: The brief calls it a pursuer made of light; matte rust bodies with a single heart glow lose legibility against the amber core chamber and stop lighting the floor.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the hunched stalking pose, but make the body emissive white-gold like A's so it blooms and pools on the floor; remove the dark halo behind them.

top_issues.issue: Rimewing light does not visibly land
top_issues.why: Their glow on the ice cannot be told from the headlamp cone, so 'lit by itself in the dark' is unproven.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add small cyan point lights per wing that tint nearby ice, and stage them partly outside the beam.

top_issues.issue: Mimic spill is cold white, not its own violet
top_issues.why: The pool under it looks like a generic lamp rather than the creature's own light, which weakens the glow-that-lands rule.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Tint the mimic's light toward violet so its pool on the rock matches its body.

top_issues.issue: Long One head glow is close to clipping
top_issues.why: At play scale the head is a white-hot point; the fangs survive here, but a little more bloom would lose them.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Hold the head emissive below clipping and let the fang tips carry the brightest value.

protect: Long One as a long chain of chunky glowing segments with a fanged wedge head

why: B turns the Long One from an unreadable blown-out clump into a clear fanged serpent and sharpens the Mimic's bite. It loses some Kindled glow, which should be taken from A.
